links.outcome: Detection of performance shifts using predefined 2σ and 3σ statistical process control limits
links.effect: Model A stayed within 3σ limits for 9-13 months per organ; model B shift (p < 0.001) exceeded both thresholds for all five organs across all 7 months; 2σ more sensitive to mild deviations.
links.quote: The 2 σx¯ thresholds were more sensitive in detecting mild deviations for model A, while both limits effectively identified the substantial drift of model B.

links.outcome: Monthly monitoring of auto-segmentation agreement with clinical contours for drift
links.effect: Monthly monitoring detected model switch/practice change; no degradation trend or clinician overreliance observed over 20 months; authors recommend at least monthly QA.
links.quote: The monitoring system effectively detected out-of-distribution outliers and clinical practice changes, providing a reliable framework for early detection of monthly performance degradation.

links.outcome: Flagging of out-of-distribution outlier cases (e.g., metal artifacts)
links.effect: Flagged prostate outliers included 5 cases with fiducials and 6 with hip implants; rectum, bladder, femoral head outliers attributed to metal artifacts and generalization limits.
links.quote: By employing statistical process control, our framework effectively identified out-of-distribution outliers, serving as an early warning mechanism to prevent performance degradation.

links.outcome: Apparent accuracy differences associated with clinician-edited AI reference contours
links.effect: Mean DSC increased from 0.82–0.96 to 0.89–0.97; HD95 decreased from 5.0–9.6 mm to 2.5–5.7 mm. Clinical references were edited AI outputs; authors cautioned that improved agreement did not necessarily indicate intrinsically better performance.
links.quote: The mean DSC increased from a range of 0.82–0.96 during testing to 0.89–0.97 during clinical practice, while the HD95 decreased from 5.0–9.6 mm to 2.5–5.7 mm across all organs of interest.

links.outcome: Detection of temporal segmentation-performance shifts using monthly control charts
links.effect: Retrospective monitoring used 150 baseline and 314 validation cases and detected model-switching shifts (p < 0.001). Model A remained within 3 σx¯ limits for 9-13 months per organ. No obvious degradation was observed.
links.quote: Model B showed systematic deviations from baseline performance, with monthly averages exceeding the established control limits for every organ.

links.outcome: Segmentation outliers associated with image artifacts and implanted materials
links.effect: Among prostate outliers, five cases were associated with fiducials and six with hip implants. Many other patients with fiducials remained within acceptable thresholds; hip-prosthesis metal artifacts also contributed to femoral-head segmentation failures.
links.quote: Among the prostate outliers, five cases were associated with fiducials and six with hip implants.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of predefined control thresholds to performance deviations
links.effect: 2 σx¯ thresholds detected mild deviations more sensitively than 3 σx¯ thresholds; both detected the substantial shift associated with model B.
links.quote: The 2 σx¯ thresholds were more sensitive in detecting mild deviations for model A, while both limits effectively identified the substantial drift of model B.

links.effect: The 2 standard deviation limits detected mild deviations more sensitively, and both limits successfully identified substantial drift.
links.quote: The 2 σx¯ thresholds were more sensitive in detecting mild deviations for model A, while both limits effectively identified the substantial drift of model B.

links.effect: The performance monitoring framework successfully detected outliers and shifts in clinical practice over time.
links.quote: The monitoring system effectively detected out-of-distribution outliers and clinical practice changes, providing a reliable framework for early detection of monthly performance degradation.
